what: THE ONE DECLARATION of the heavy-run launch form's constants. Every literal in code that names these values reads this file or asserts equality with it in its selftest; two definitions of the conflict code (be_heavy_run.sh:36 and be_rule22.py:134) and two bare literals were measured drifting-capable at REV 67 §2.3 (a launcher refusing with 76 was published as 75).
lock_conflict_rc_why: flock -E 75: a held lock exits with the declared code, distinct from any payload exit; without -E a refusal and a crash are both ExecMainStatus=1 (REV 67 §2.1, measured). No runner or producer may exit 75 for any other reason; each declares its own exit codes and asserts 75 is not among them.
unit_outcome_note: read the FIVE fields while LoadState=loaded and COPY them with the unit's InvocationID at once; LoadState=not-found makes the rest defaults and the reading VOID; under RemainAfterExit=yes a FINISHED unit is loaded/active/EXITED and a RUNNING one loaded/active/RUNNING with ExecMainStatus 0 in both — SubState is the discriminator; a killed or OOM-killed unit reports Result=signal with ExecMainStatus = the signal number (not in any exit map); THE PROPERTY-SIDE TIE (REV 69 §3.5): InvocationID is non-empty only while the unit is loaded and empty after stop or collection, so a copy carrying a non-empty InvocationID could only have been taken while the unit existed — a copy without one is VOID whatever its LoadState string says; after the receipt lands and the five fields + id are copied, the owner stops the unit (MemoryPeak and InvocationID are retained while loaded/exited and [not set]/empty after stop — copy BEFORE stopping); a unit name that is still loaded (active/exited OR failed) makes systemd-run FAIL at launch ('already loaded') — unique names per launch, reset-failed/stop hygiene by the owner

journal_identity.cross_check: journalctl --user -u <unit> -o cat | wc -l must equal the by-id count for a unit launched once under that name
journal_identity.measured: de95smoke.service: 1 line (the Started line, USER_INVOCATION_ID only); be64book.service: 99 manager lines (USER_INVOCATION_ID), 26 payload lines (_SYSTEMD_INVOCATION_ID), 1 neither — 13:37Z; a unit NAME names every run ever launched under it
journal_identity.note: a copy that returns 0 lines for a unit whose -u query has lines is a REFUSAL of the copy, never a record (two coordinator copies were exactly that, 13:35Z/13:36Z, deleted)

decidable_launch_form_property: the process's own cgroup leaf suffix from /proc/self/cgroup: '.service' admits a real day, '.scope' refuses it (DE 96 assert_launch_form_at_runtime); the PPid test in the runbook is the OUTSIDE diagnostic and holds of MainPID (flock), not of the payload (a grandchild)

supersedes.why: v2's three-field minimum read is insufficient under the RemainAfterExit it declares: RUNNING and FINISHED are both loaded/active/0 (measured, REV 69 §3.3); SubState discriminates (running vs exited) and Result carries the signal case (Result=signal, ExecMainStatus=<signal number>, REV 69 §1.3)

remain_after_exit_why: with RemainAfterExit=yes a unit that exits 0 stays LOADED as active/exited with ExecMainStatus 0 and Result success until `systemctl --user stop <unit>`; the lock is a process-held flock and is released when the payload exits regardless of the unit object. Measured 13:48Z: exit 0 without it -> not-found/inactive/dead/0/success (defaults); exit 3 without it -> loaded/failed/3; exit 0 with it -> loaded/active/exited/0/success; exit 3 with it -> loaded/failed/3.
chain_head_rule: readers resolve THE CHAIN HEAD of heavy_run_form_v*.json in this directory (the newest version whose supersedes pair {path, sha256} verifies against the file it names, back to v1) — never a filename literal; a reader pinned to a superseded version satisfies the words of rule 20's guard 1 without the property (REV 69 §3.1/§4: the runner pinned v1 at 14:00Z while v2 existed)
runtime_form_check: the -E half is decidable at runtime exactly as the --scope half is: the payload's parent IS flock, so /proc/<PPid>/cmdline carries 'flock -n -E <rc> <lock_path> ...' — a runner asserts its own parent's cmdline against this declaration (REV 69 §1.2); the composed-string lint is a lint
grounding_drive: exactly ONE drive grounds the conflict code's BEHAVIOUR: a unit launched against a HELD scratch lock with a payload whose own exit map excludes 75, its five fields and InvocationID read while loaded and copied into the launcher owner's receipt (REV 69 §4 guard 3); the declared lock_path is grounded separately by inode (wrapper_observed), never by that drive
